privacy.audioLocal: What you play stays on your device. We never send or store audio.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: Klavio only keeps what you need for learning – and the sound of your piano never leaves your device. Here is, in plain words, what is stored where.

items.1: What the microphone hears is only analysed on your device – never recorded, uploaded or stored.
items.2: No ads, no tracking, no analytics, no tracking cookies.
items.3: No birthdate – only the year of birth, so Klavio offers the right worlds. No location, and children need no e-mail address of their own.
items.4: You can see, change and delete everything yourself in the app.

responsible.title: Who is responsible?
responsible.text: {{name}} is responsible for the data in this Klavio instance.
responsible.unknown: Whoever runs this Klavio instance is responsible. The contact details have not been filled in yet – ask the person who recommended Klavio to you.
responsible.software: {{app}} is free software. Its developers get no data from this instance.

audio.title: Microphone and sound
audio.text: Klavio listens through the microphone to hear which key you play. This happens right in the browser: only numbers like pitch and loudness are worked out, and they stay on the page too. There is no recording, no upload and no storage of sound.

items.1: With a digital piano over MIDI or the on-screen keyboard, Klavio needs no microphone at all.
items.2: «Klavi reads aloud» only uses voices installed on your device. The text goes to no service.

stored.title: What is stored on the server
stored.text: So that you can keep learning on several devices, the server keeps:

items.1: Account: a name (e.g. «The Smiths»), your e-mail address, whether you are an admin and – if set – an encrypted parent PIN.
items.2: Passkeys: only the public key and details like the name of the password manager. Fingerprint, face and private keys stay on your device.
items.3: Profiles: name or nickname, year of birth, figure, view and world, daily goal, microphone setting, XP, level, streak, badges and – if chosen – the title of your dream song.
items.4: Learning progress: stars and reviews per lesson and the practice time per day.
items.5: Server log: time, address called and answer – without IP addresses.

device.title: What is stored on your device
device.text: Klavio sets only two cookies, both technically necessary: one keeps you signed in, one protects signing in with a passkey. The browser's storage keeps your latest state (so Klavio also works offline), results not sent yet and settings like language and colour scheme. Signing out deletes your state from the device.

sharing.title: Who gets data
sharing.text: Klavio loads nothing from other servers – fonts and music notation come from here too.

items.1: The e-mail provider of this instance sends your codes and sees your address and the code.
items.2: Whoever runs the server (hosting) technically has access to the data.
items.3: Nobody else: no advertising, analytics or crash-reporting services.

items.1: Account, profiles and progress: until you delete them.
items.2: You stay signed in for 60 days, then you sign in again.
items.4: Backups keep data until they expire – the operator decides how long.
items.5: If the operator has set it: accounts unused for a long time are deleted after a warning by e-mail.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: You can see, change and delete your data yourself at any time:

items.1: Account, passkeys, profiles, progress and badges are right there in the app.
items.2: Change name, e-mail address and profiles under «Account» and «Profile».
items.3: «Delete account» under «Account» immediately removes account, passkeys, profiles and progress.
items.4: For anything else, write to the operator. You can also complain to the data protection authority – in Switzerland the FDPIC.
items.5: Under «Account → Download data» you get everything stored about your account as a file.

children.title: Children
children.text: Children learn with a profile in an adult's account and need no e-mail address of their own; the name can be a nickname. With the parent PIN (or a passkey) you decide who may change the account, profiles and settings.

piano.q: Do I need a digital piano?
piano.a: No. A real piano is enough – the microphone recognises the notes. You can connect a digital piano via USB MIDI, and there is an on-screen keyboard to try things out.

who.a: For children and adults without prior knowledge. Everyone gets their own profile – children a playful look, adults a calm one if they like.

devices.q: Which devices does Klavio run on?
devices.a: In any current browser on a tablet, phone or computer. You can also install Klavio like an app.

offline.a: Yes. Lessons work offline, and your results are sent as soon as you're back online.

cost.a: Nothing. Klavio is free, with no subscription, no ads and no hidden purchases. It is free software: anyone can also run it themselves.

adults.a: No. Adults choose the calmer «Classic» view and the world «The journey» with its elevation profile and dream song. The lessons are the same, without the kids' stuff.

landing.journeyTitle: The journey to your dream song
landing.journeyText: Learning the piano is not a straight road: first it goes gently downhill, then it gets steep – and at some point comes hell, the hardest part. Klavio tells you before you get there and shows you on an elevation profile where you are.

landing.hostTitle: For families, schools and music schools: run it yourself
landing.hostText: Klavio is free software. With one Docker image it runs on your own server – just for your family, your class or your music school, with your own e-mails and without any data leaving the house.

journey.title: Four stages to your dream song

phase.start: Right now you’re laying the foundations: keys, right hand, first notes. After that it gets tough for a while – that’s part of it and it passes. Every lesson brings you closer to {{goal}}.
phase.grind: You’re in the hard stretch. Tough feels like standing still, but it is progress. Stick to your weekly goal – that’s how you get through.
phase.climb: The toughest part is behind you. Now both hands play together, and with every chapter it sounds more like music.
phase.summit: The last stage: keys, accompaniment and expression. Afterwards you have the basics for {{goal}} – the piece itself you then practise step by step.
phase.done: Summit reached! You can now do everything Klavio teaches. Get the sheet music of {{goal}} yourself – then practise it piece by piece, with the metronome.

journey.estimate_one: With {{days}} practice days a week you’ll be at the top in about {{count}} week – if you manage one lesson per practice day.

journey.survived: You kept going! The hard stretch is behind you.

help.tips: Klavi’s tips in the exercise show you what matters.
help.short: Short every day beats long once: 10 minutes are enough.
